title: Computer and Information Sciences Skeleton v1
description: Coverage skeleton for the computer-and-information-sciences continent (third continent, CPO-selected 2026-06-11, vault decision log (23)): field/subfield two-level node set under domain:computer-and-information-sciences — computing areas and the library-and-information-science wing — each tagged with academic_status. Construction input only — not canonical graph data; nodes only, zero edges (skeleton-first). The three junction nodes already canonical in /data (domain:computer-and-information-sciences, field:computer-science, field:machine-learning) are out of generation scope; field:machine-learning carries a standing structural question (level-1 field legacy) reserved for QC.

include: Computer and information sciences field and subfield coverage skeleton (nodes only)
Computing areas under LCC QA75.5-76.95, UDC 004, ACM CCS 2012, MSC 68, and FORD 1.2, including historical and applied areas
Library and information science wing (LCC Z665-718.8, UDC 02), every candidate gated case-by-case by the section-12 dual criterion and cross-continent assignment rule
Cryptography transfer acceptance (section-12 precedent 2026-06-10: cryptography deferred from formal sciences to CS)
Wikidata QID resolution for identity and external_ids
exclude: Edges and relations (skeleton-first: dots before lines; part_of skeleton edges are a separate batch)
Re-proposing any existing /data node (the three CS junction nodes and all 125 other canonical nodes; reconcile to existing IDs instead)

Formal-sciences areas already canonical (computability-theory, information-theory, game-theory stay under formal sciences; their CS-targeted second memberships are a separate cross-listing task under section 13)
Electrical and computer engineering hardware areas whose primary LCC home (TK) and dominant institutional home are both engineering
Living computer scientists and current affiliations

seed_entities.label: Machine learning
seed_entities.notes: Existing /data node (reviewed, Q2539, ML-foundations legacy). Not a generation target; listed as the continent's standing structural question for QC — level-1 field under a part_of parent (mathematical-logic field-to-subfield demotion precedent applies or is distinguished at QC).

allowed_public_sources.notes: CC0. Resolver verifies the unverified training-knowledge QID hints in the proposal and fills missing QIDs.
External-link / source-resolution pointer only. Never store or cache article bodies.

forbidden_sources.reason: NamuWiki is external-link-only and must never be used as evidence or a source, nor have its content cached.
No cloud LLM API calls are permitted in repo tooling, build, validation, or runtime.
Scraping or crawling third-party article bodies is forbidden; only open, license-compatible data is allowed.

notes: Continent selection and scope ratified by the CPO 2026-06-11 (vault decision log (23)).

Coverage baseline for generation/QC: LCC QA75.5-76.95 and Z665-718.8 (outline PDF + id.loc.gov authority records), UDC 004 and 02 (UDC Summary), ACM CCS 2012 (dl.acm.org; Wayback fallback if bot-blocked, access path recorded), with MSC 2020 section 68 and OECD FORD 1.2 as cross-checks and the arXiv cs.* category taxonomy as an auxiliary cross-check only.
docs/data-foundry.md section 12 (including its precedent log) is a mandatory input to the generation order (promotion policy v1.3); section 13 governs any multi-membership question raised during QC.

Known structural questions pre-registered for QC: (1) field:machine-learning level-1 field legacy vs the mathematical-logic field-to-subfield demotion precedent; (2) cryptography transfer acceptance; (3) the information-sciences wing is gated case-by-case by the section-12 dual test — escalated only if it proves a policy question.

The initial seed list is provisional (the standing structural-question target only); the full seed list is regenerated mechanically from the QC-passed proposal.json before the resolver pass (formal-sciences precedent, PR #30).
/data remains the source of truth for accepted graph data.
